name: padic_units_distance_le_max
source: private theorem padic_units_distance_le_max (l : ℕ) [Fact l.Prime] (a b : ℤ_[l]) (ha : ‖a‖ = 1) (hb : ‖b‖ = 1)
‖a - b‖ ≤ max ‖algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (a : ℚ_[l]) * z - 1‖
set A := algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (a : ℚ_[l])
set B := algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (b : ℚ_[l])
simp only [A, B, ← map_sub, PadicAlgCl.norm_extends, ← PadicInt.coe_sub, ← PadicInt.norm_def]
have hdiff : A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1) = (A - B) * z := by ring
have hmax : ‖A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1)‖ ≤ max ‖A * z - 1‖ ‖B * z - 1‖ := by
_ = ‖A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1)‖ := by rw [hdiff, norm_mul, hAB]
· have hAz : ‖A * z‖ < 1 := by rw [norm_mul, hA, one_mul]; exact hz
rw [norm_neg, show A * z + -(A * z - 1) = 1 by ring, norm_one] at this
rcases le_max_iff.mp this with h | h
show: For ℓ-adic integers a and b of norm one and any z in the algebraic closure of the ℓ-adics, the distance between a and b is at most the larger of the distances of az and bz from one, with a and b embedded in the closure.
strategy: Subtract the two residuals and apply the ultrametric inequality. When z has small norm, the residual from a unit already has norm one.

steps.claim: Write $A,B$ for the images of the $\ell$-adic integers $a,b$ in $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, using $\mathbf Z_\ell\subseteq\mathbf Q_\ell$. Both products with the given $z$ are then taken in this field.
steps.snippet:
‖algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (b : ℚ_[l]) * z - 1‖ := by
  set A := algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (a : ℚ_[l])
  set B := algebraMap ℚ_[l] (PadicAlgCl l) (b : ℚ_[l])

steps.claim: The norm on $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ extends the $\ell$-adic norm, so $\lVert A\rVert=\lVert a\rVert=1$.
steps.snippet:
have hA : ‖A‖ = 1 := by
    simp only [A, PadicAlgCl.norm_extends, ← PadicInt.norm_def, ha]

steps.claim: The embeddings preserve subtraction and the norm, giving $\lVert A-B\rVert=\lVert a-b\rVert$.
steps.snippet:
have hAB : ‖A - B‖ = ‖a - b‖ := by
    simp only [A, B, ← map_sub, PadicAlgCl.norm_extends, ← PadicInt.coe_sub, ← PadicInt.norm_def]

steps.claim: Subtracting the two residuals cancels their constant terms and gives $(Az-1)-(Bz-1)=(A-B)z$.
steps.snippet: have hdiff : A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1) = (A - B) * z := by ring

steps.claim: The ultrametric inequality gives $\lVert (Az-1)-(Bz-1)\rVert\le\max(\lVert Az-1\rVert,\lVert Bz-1\rVert)$, since negation preserves the norm.
steps.snippet:
have hmax : ‖A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1)‖ ≤ max ‖A * z - 1‖ ‖B * z - 1‖ := by
    have := IsUltrametricDist.norm_add_le_max (A * z - 1) (-(B * z - 1))
    rwa [norm_neg, ← sub_eq_add_neg] at this

steps.claim: When $\lVert z\rVert\ge1$ the norm of $(A-B)z$ bounds $\lVert a-b\rVert$. When $\lVert z\rVert<1$ the residual $Az-1$ already has norm at least $1$.

children.claim: If $\lVert z\rVert\ge1$, then $\lVert a-b\rVert\le\lVert a-b\rVert\lVert z\rVert=\lVert (Az-1)-(Bz-1)\rVert$, and the ultrametric inequality bounds the last norm by the larger residual.
children.snippet:
· calc ‖a - b‖ ≤ ‖a - b‖ * ‖z‖ := le_mul_of_one_le_right (norm_nonneg _) hz
      _ = ‖A * z - 1 - (B * z - 1)‖ := by rw [hdiff, norm_mul, hAB]
      _ ≤ _ := hmax

children.claim: If $\lVert z\rVert<1$, then $\lVert Az\rVert<1$. Writing $1=Az-(Az-1)$ forces $\lVert Az-1\rVert\ge1$ by the ultrametric inequality, while $\lVert a-b\rVert\le1$ since $a-b\in\mathbf Z_\ell$.
children.snippet: · have hAz : ‖A * z‖ < 1 := by rw [norm_mul, hA, one_mul]; exact hz

children.claim: Multiplicativity and $\lVert A\rVert=1$ give $\lVert Az\rVert=\lVert z\rVert<1$.
children.snippet: · have hAz : ‖A * z‖ < 1 := by rw [norm_mul, hA, one_mul]; exact hz

children.claim: The residual satisfies $\lVert Az-1\rVert\ge1$. Indeed, $\lVert1\rVert\le\max(\lVert Az\rVert,\lVert Az-1\rVert)$ and the first entry is strictly smaller than $1$.
The ultrametric inequality for $Az$ and $-(Az-1)$ bounds the norm of their sum by the maximum of their norms.
The sum on the left is $1$ and the norm is invariant under negation. Thus the inequality reads $1\le\max(\lVert Az\rVert,\lVert Az-1\rVert)$.
children.snippet: rw [norm_neg, show A * z + -(A * z - 1) = 1 by ring, norm_one] at this

children.claim: Cancelling $Az$ against $-Az$ gives the ring identity $Az+(-(Az-1))=1$.
children.snippet: rw [norm_neg, show A * z + -(A * z - 1) = 1 by ring, norm_one] at this

children.claim: For the maximum of two real numbers to be at least $1$, at least one of $\lVert Az\rVert$ and $\lVert Az-1\rVert$ must be at least $1$.
children.snippet: rcases le_max_iff.mp this with h | h

children.claim: The remaining alternative gives $1\le\lVert Az-1\rVert$, the required lower bound.
Every $\ell$-adic integer has norm at most one. Therefore $\lVert a-b\rVert\le1\le\lVert Az-1\rVert\le\max(\lVert Az-1\rVert,\lVert Bz-1\rVert)$.
children.snippet:
calc ‖a - b‖ ≤ 1 := PadicInt.norm_le_one _
      _ ≤ ‖A * z - 1‖ := h1
      _ ≤ _ := le_max_left _ _

chapterTitle: Twisted cokernels in a cyclotomic tower
